title: fix(plugin-*,components): one record-overlay shell honouring all four `navigation.mode` values
body:
Fixes #9299

Implements the director-seat ruling of decision batch #128 item 1 (2026-09-13): one shared overlay shell, so the four declared overlay `navigation.mode` values mean the same thing on every list-type renderer.

`RecordDetailDrawer`'s payload — `InlineEditProvider` wrapping `DetailView` plus `InlineEditSaveBar`, and the objectSchema-to-typed-field derivation that feeds them — is extracted into a new shell-free `RecordDetailPanel` and mounted through `NavigationOverlay` by `ObjectGrid`, `ObjectTree`, `ObjectGantt`, `ObjectKanban` and `ObjectCalendar`. `RecordDetailDrawer` keeps its published props and is now a thin wrapper over the same shell in `drawer` mode, which is what makes item 4 literally true: there is one drag-resize implementation left, not two. No spec change (`Clause-2: no`, declared by the ruling itself).

## What each ruled item became

| Item | Where |
|---|---|
| 1 — one shared overlay shell | `packages/plugin-detail/src/RecordDetailPanel.tsx` (new), `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` (delegates), five renderers |
| 2 — `split` gets each renderer's own view as `mainContent` | every renderer's `renderRecordOverlay(mainContent)` |
| 3 — `popover` anchored to the clicked element | `popoverAnchorRef` + `useOverlayAnchor` in `navigation-overlay.tsx` |
| 4 — one resize store, migrated not reset | `useDrawerResize`'s `legacyStorageKey` read |
| 5 — no spec change, no dev-only warning | nothing in `packages/types` or `@objectstack/spec` moved |

## The `popover` mechanism, and why it is not `popoverTrigger`

The ruling names `popoverTrigger` as the vehicle for "anchored to the clicked element". Measured: that prop cannot carry it. It is rendered through Radix's `PopoverTrigger asChild`, which MOUNTS its child inside the overlay's own subtree — so handing it the clicked row would draw a **second copy of that row** inside the popover rather than point at the first. The element the popover must anchor to is one the renderer already drew somewhere else entirely.

So the ruled BEHAVIOUR is delivered through the shape Radix publishes for exactly this case — a virtual anchor (`Popper.Anchor virtualRef`) behind a new `popoverAnchorRef` prop. `popoverTrigger` is untouched and still works for a host that wants the overlay to render its own trigger. The `Dialog` fallback now requires BOTH to be absent, and none of the five reaches it.

A vehicle that provably cannot carry the ruled behaviour is a measurement, not a licence to change the behaviour — and the behaviour is unchanged.

## Two things the card did not know, both measured here

**1. `ObjectGrid`'s `split` was blank too.** The card calls `ObjectGrid` one of the two renderers that get overlay modes right, and says the `split` blank is an `ObjectTree` problem because the grid passes `mainContent` "via a dedicated early return". The measurement checked that the prop is PASSED, never that the closed state renders. It does not: the grid entered its split path on the authored mode alone, while the shell's split branch opens `if (!isOpen || !mainContent) return null` — so a grid authored `split` rendered nothing at all, and nothing could ever be clicked to open it. Same defect class as the `ObjectTree` blank, on the renderer the card calls correct. Repaired here (item 2 names no exception), and pinned by the mount step of every `split` case in the five new shell-mode files.

**2. The shared payload needs DECLARED fields, so grid and tree keep their own reading when there are none.** `RecordDetailPanel` renders the object's declared fields; `ObjectGrid` and `ObjectTree` render the same values by INFERRING from them — a date-shaped string on a `*_date` key, a currency-ish number on an `amount` key — which is what objectui#4541 (locale-aware date fallback), objectui#8491 (the localized `Empty` placeholder) and objectui#8920 (the `format` hint) put there. With the payload ungated, `recordDetailDateLocale` read back `close_date2024-03-15` in a zh session: three landed behaviours regressing for any grid over inline `value` rows or a DataSource with no `getObjectSchema`.

So those two renderers take the shared payload wherever the object declares its fields — every console surface — and keep their inference reading where there is nothing to declare.

⭐ **This is a payload-CONTENT deviation only, and it is pinned as such rather than asserted.** On the no-schema path the overlay is still `NavigationOverlay`, it still receives all four authored modes as four distinct boundary pairs, `split` still gets `mainContent` and `popover` still gets the clicked element — driven, not read off the call graph, in the closing `describe` of `ObjectGrid.overlayShellModes-9299.test.tsx` (with a lit control proving that mount really does take the fallback branch) and again in `ObjectTree.overlayShellModes-9299.test.tsx`, where a schema-less tree is the common case rather than an edge.

## Consequences on published surfaces, stated rather than discovered

- **Drawer chrome converges** for gantt / kanban / calendar on the shared shell's header (breadcrumb-style title, close, optional expand) in place of the sr-only `SheetHeader`. This is the "chrome de-duplication" route (a) priced in. The shell also adopts `RecordDetailDrawer`'s deliberate `onOpenAutoFocus` suppression, so the grid and tree drawers stop flashing a focus ring on open.
- **Default width is unchanged at every viewport.** The shell expresses an authored width as a floor, `max(WIDTH, min(60vw, 880px))`, and for the ruled default `min(960px, 60vw)` that reduces to `min(960px, 60vw)` at every viewport — the three `navWidthDefault` pins assert the reduced expression and carry the arithmetic. objectui#6584 holds.
- **An authored width below `min(60vw, 880px)` now widens to it** on gantt / kanban / calendar. That is the shell's long-standing policy on grid and tree; converging on one shell means converging on one width policy. Pinned explicitly (`an authored navigation.width still reaches the shell unchanged`).
- **Mobile**: below the `sm` breakpoint the overlay occupies the full viewport instead of the authored width, which is the shell's documented mobile behaviour.
- **Grid and tree overlays now issue the record's `POST /api/v1/security/explain` read** (two per open) because `DetailView` asks whether the record may be updated and deleted. That call is `DetailView`'s, ungated by `inlineEdit`, and pre-existing on the three renderers that already rendered this payload; it is noted, not changed here.
- **Richer record body on grid and tree** wherever fields are declared: typed widgets, declared labels, honoured `hidden`, the object's own field order.

## Item 4 — the migration, proved from an existing width

`packages/components/src/__tests__/navigation-overlay-9299.test.tsx` seeds `objectui.drawerWidth.contacts = 640` with the new key ABSENT, then reads back that 640px is what the overlay renders, that `ov:drawer-width:contacts` now holds it, and that the retired key is gone — a migration proof rather than a new-key proof. Plus: a stale-legacy-loses case, a no-persisted-width control, a below-floor case, and a pin on both key spellings. The surviving floor is the LOWER of the two (360 vs 480), so no width either implementation could have written is discarded.

## Reverse verification (one-time, not left in the tree)

Both new shell mechanisms were ablated at HEAD with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap, the mutation proved on disk by a grep count in both directions, and the restore proved by blob hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD`:

| Ablation | Mutation landed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| delete the legacy-key migration read | `legacyRaw` 3 hits to 0, marker injected | 1 failed / 7 passed — `starts from an EXISTING persisted width` red: `expected 'max(min(960px, 60vw), min(60vw, 880px))' to be '640px'`, i.e. exactly the silent reset the ruling forbids |
| widen the popover fallback guard to ignore `popoverAnchorRef` | guard 1 hit to 0, marker injected | 2 failed / 6 passed — both anchor cases red |

## Test files: replaced, not kept

The four objectui#9113 measurement files pin the branch this card deleted (`RecordDetailDrawer:undefined` four times over, and on `ObjectTree` a `split` that renders nothing and a `popover` with no anchor). They are replaced by `*.overlayShellModes-9299.test.tsx` on all five renderers, reusing the same two instruments so the two rounds are comparable — the hook spy and the shell recorder used to DISAGREE, and the disagreement was the defect; they agree now. Assertions stay on the mode VALUE because `sheet.tsx` and `dialog.tsx` both render the same Radix role with no `data-slot`, so a DOM assertion is blind to this defect by construction.

Three `navWidthDefault` files move their reading from the panel's inline `max-width` to the `--ov-w` custom property the shell publishes; reading `style.maxWidth` there would return an empty string in both worlds and pin nothing.

A shared `installRecordSecurityExplainDouble` lands in the private `@object-ui/test-support` so the seven files whose renders now reach `DetailView` serve that read from a recording double instead of a real socket — it records every URL and fails on anything that is not the explain route, so an escape elsewhere reds where it happens.

## Verification

All runs at `69fe1e7` unless noted; test suites through the shared verify lock.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm lint` (whole repo, 47 packages) | exit 0 — 47/47 tasks, 0 errors |
| `turbo run type-check` (7 changed packages + test-support) | exit 0 — 22/22 tasks |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-grid/ packages/plugin-tree/` | 146 files / 1288 tests passed |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/` | 69 files / 538 tests passed |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/ packages/plugin-calendar/` | 91 files / 609 tests passed |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` | 175 files / 1625 tests passed |
| `vitest run packages/components/ packages/test-support/` | 277 files / 2692 tests passed |
| gates | `check:control-bytes`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:dist-completeness`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:published-dist`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:lint-rule-coverage`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:readme-exports`, `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-examples`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:changeset-claims`, changeset presence + no-major — all exit 0 |
| NOT MEASURED locally | `check:eager-closure` and `check:sdui-registration-pins` both exit 2 (PRECONDITION NOT MET — they weigh `apps/console/dist`, which needs a console build). Neither is a failure reading; CI's `Build & E2E` builds it. |

The grid/tree, detail and components suite numbers were taken at `4d9bb7e`; the only commits since touch a gantt test file (deleted), one components test file (re-run green at HEAD, 8/8) and two doc files, none of which those suites read.

`Bundle Analysis` is red on `origin/main`'s own tip and on every PR from this lane; it is outside the required nine and is not this PR's.
